# Week 16: Consolidation and capstone planning {.unnumbered}

::: {.week-meta}
Core reading
: None

Data
: [Student Life Survey](../course/dataset.qmd) or your own data

App
: None

Task style
: Independent: plan and carry out the analysis yourself; the session reviews your plan

:::

## By the end of this week you can

- Complete a full draft of your results section.
- Assess the draft against the capstone rubric.
- Plan the capstone presentation.

## Warm-up

Answer from memory at the start of the session. It takes two minutes and makes earlier ideas easier to recall later.

1. What can you compare once scalar invariance holds?
2. What is the regression counterpart of testing equal paths across groups?
3. Why bootstrap an indirect effect?

<details class="answers">
<summary>Check your answers</summary>

1. Latent means.
2. A group × predictor interaction.
3. Its sampling distribution is skewed.

</details>

## This week in brief

No new material. You finish your results draft, assess it against the rubric, and plan the capstone. Bring the draft to the session.

## Before the session

Make sure every section of your draft exists, even in rough form: screening and missing data, measurement model, structural model, group comparisons. Polishing comes in Week 16, using the rubric.

## In the session

- Your self-assessment against the rubric, and our comments.
- What to present in Week 17, and in what order.

## Your task this week

1. Assess your draft against the [rubric](week-17.qmd#capstone-rubric). For each criterion, note what is missing.
2. Revise the draft.
3. Plan a 15-minute presentation of your analysis.

::: {.callout-note title="Before next week's session"}
Week 17 has no new material, so prepare for it during this week. Finalise your draft and presentation. Use the reporting checklist in @schreiber2006 and the APA standards.
:::

## For your SEM log

Write your answers in your log first; then compare.

1. Which rubric criterion is your draft weakest on?
2. What would a reviewer most likely question about your analysis?

<details class="answers model">
<summary>Compare with model answers (after writing your own)</summary>

1. Answers vary. Common gaps are justifying respecifications and reporting enough detail for someone else to reproduce the analysis.
2. Answers vary. Typical targets: causal language with cross-sectional data, post hoc changes, and the handling of missing data.

</details>

## Checkpoint

Before the capstone:

- [ ] My results draft covers screening, missing data, the measurement model, the structural model and group comparisons.
- [ ] Every respecification is justified.
- [ ] I can explain every number in my tables.
- [ ] I have checked the draft against the rubric.

Anything you cannot yet tick is the first item for the next session.

## Extra resources

Optional. Each is labelled with when it is worth reading.

- **Reporting standards:** @appelbaum2018, the SEM section of the APA Journal Article Reporting Standards.
